## Story-level uncertainties

- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the son is called Kanaan or Yam, and later works add details of his age and conduct.
- The ayat do not say whether the son was a believer at any time, and the meaning of not of your family is read in different ways.
- Hadith to add later: reports about Nuh's son and the passage 11:45-47, with a named grader for each; none is used here.

## How to review

1. Verses: do the listed ayat really contain what each claim says? Is any claim stronger than its ayat?
2. Pronouns and speakers: where the Arabic names none, does the draft say so?
3. Words with more than one reading: decide how the page words each.
4. Omissions: anything the verses say that readers need and the chapter leaves out?
5. No added facts: no name, number, place, reason, emotion or sequence beyond the ayat; no implied chronology.
6. No depiction of any prophet, angel or jinn.
7. Theology and etiquette: cautious wording about prophets; no verdicts; no legal or medical ruling.
8. Kids mode only restates the claims; nothing frightening or misleading.
9. Lessons are marked as interpretation and are modest; none reads as scripture or a promise.
10. Unknowns and tradition: each 'Named in later tradition' line is accurate and only a label.
11. Titles and honorifics: bare names in the draft; honorifics added at render time.
12. Sign-off goes in the platform review flow (name, version, decision), not in this file.

## 1. The son who stayed apart  (`#the-son-who-stayed-apart`)

Cited ayat: 11:42-43

> **11:42** وَهِىَ تَجْرِى بِهِمْ فِى مَوْجٍ كَٱلْجِبَالِ وَنَادَىٰ نُوحٌ ٱبْنَهُۥ وَكَانَ فِى مَعْزِلٍ يَٰبُنَىَّ ٱرْكَب مَّعَنَا وَلَا تَكُن مَّعَ ٱلْكَٰفِرِينَ
>
> **11:43** قَالَ سَـَٔاوِىٓ إِلَىٰ جَبَلٍ يَعْصِمُنِى مِنَ ٱلْمَآءِ قَالَ لَا عَاصِمَ ٱلْيَوْمَ مِنْ أَمْرِ ٱللَّهِ إِلَّا مَن رَّحِمَ وَحَالَ بَيْنَهُمَا ٱلْمَوْجُ فَكَانَ مِنَ ٱلْمُغْرَقِينَ

### Claims

**c1** (11:42): While the ship ran with them through waves like mountains, Nuh called to his son, who was standing apart, and told him to come aboard with them and not to be with the disbelievers.

**c2** (11:43): The son answered that he would take refuge on a mountain that would protect him from the water.

**c3** (11:43): The reply was that today there is no protector from the command of God, except for the one on whom He has mercy.

**c4** (11:43): The waves came between them, and the son was among the drowned.

### One-minute summary

Nuh called to his son and told him to come aboard and not be with the disbelievers [c1]. The son answered that a mountain would protect him from the water, but the waves came between them and he was among the drowned [c2][c4].

### Complete story

While the ship ran with them through waves like mountains, Nuh called to his son, who was standing apart, and told him to come aboard with them and not to be with the disbelievers [c1]. The son answered that he would take refuge on a mountain that would protect him from the water [c2]. The reply was that today there is no protector from the command of God, except for the one on whom He has mercy [c3]. The waves came between them, and the son was among the drowned [c4].

### Deep study

The ayah gives the son's answer and then a reply that no one is protected from God's command except those on whom He has mercy [c3]. It does not say who gave that reply, although it follows Nuh's call [c3].

### Kids mode

Nuh called to his son to come aboard the ship [c1]. The son said a mountain would keep him safe [c2]. Then the waves came between them [c4].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the passage places safety in God's mercy and not in anything else [c3]. Another is that the call to come aboard was an invitation that the son did not accept [c1][c2].

### What the sources do not establish

- Not established: the name or age of the son, or whether he had heard Nuh's call before this moment.
- The ayah says only that it ran; the ship is named in the previous ayah (11:41), which lies outside the verses of this item.
- Not established: who spoke the reply about the command of God; the ayah does not mark the speaker.
- Not established: where the mountain was, or whether the son reached it.

## 2. Nuh's plea and God's answer  (`#nuhs-plea`)

Cited ayat: 11:44-47

> **11:44** وَقِيلَ يَٰٓأَرْضُ ٱبْلَعِى مَآءَكِ وَيَٰسَمَآءُ أَقْلِعِى وَغِيضَ ٱلْمَآءُ وَقُضِىَ ٱلْأَمْرُ وَٱسْتَوَتْ عَلَى ٱلْجُودِىِّ وَقِيلَ بُعْدًا لِّلْقَوْمِ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
>
> **11:45** وَنَادَىٰ نُوحٌ رَّبَّهُۥ فَقَالَ رَبِّ إِنَّ ٱبْنِى مِنْ أَهْلِى وَإِنَّ وَعْدَكَ ٱلْحَقُّ وَأَنتَ أَحْكَمُ ٱلْحَٰكِمِينَ
>
> **11:46** قَالَ يَٰنُوحُ إِنَّهُۥ لَيْسَ مِنْ أَهْلِكَ إِنَّهُۥ عَمَلٌ غَيْرُ صَٰلِحٍ فَلَا تَسْـَٔلْنِ مَا لَيْسَ لَكَ بِهِۦ عِلْمٌ إِنِّىٓ أَعِظُكَ أَن تَكُونَ مِنَ ٱلْجَٰهِلِينَ
>
> **11:47** قَالَ رَبِّ إِنِّىٓ أَعُوذُ بِكَ أَنْ أَسْـَٔلَكَ مَا لَيْسَ لِى بِهِۦ عِلْمٌ وَإِلَّا تَغْفِرْ لِى وَتَرْحَمْنِىٓ أَكُن مِّنَ ٱلْخَٰسِرِينَ

### Claims

**c1** (11:44): The earth was told to swallow its water and the sky to hold back, the water subsided, the matter was decided, and the ship came to rest on the Judi.

**c2** (11:44): The ayah adds a word of rejection for the wrongdoing people.

**c3** (11:45): Nuh called to his Lord and said that his son was of his family, that God's promise is true, and that God is the most just of judges.

**c4** (11:46): God told Nuh that the son was not of his family, describing him with the words an unrighteous deed, and told him not to ask Him about what he had no knowledge of, warning him not to be among the ignorant.

**c5** (11:47): Nuh answered that he sought refuge in God from asking about what he had no knowledge of, and that unless God forgave him and had mercy on him, he would be among the losers.

### One-minute summary

Nuh called to his Lord that his son was of his family and that God's promise is true [c3]. God told him that the son was not of his family and told him not to ask about what he had no knowledge of [c4]. Nuh sought refuge in God from such asking and asked for forgiveness and mercy [c5].

### Complete story

The earth was told to swallow its water and the sky to hold back, the water subsided, the matter was decided, and the ship came to rest on the Judi [c1]. The ayah adds a word of rejection for the wrongdoing people [c2]. Nuh called to his Lord and said that his son was of his family, that God's promise is true, and that God is the most just of judges [c3]. God told Nuh that the son was not of his family, describing him with the words an unrighteous deed, and told him not to ask Him about what he had no knowledge of, warning him not to be among the ignorant [c4]. Nuh answered that he sought refuge in God from asking about what he had no knowledge of, and that unless God forgave him and had mercy on him, he would be among the losers [c5].

### Deep study

The words describing the son as an unrighteous deed can be read as saying that he was an unrighteous deed or that his deed was unrighteous, and the ayah is brief [c4]. The ayat do not explain the words not of your family any further [c4].

### Kids mode

The water went down and the ship came to rest [c1]. Nuh asked his Lord about his son [c3]. God told Nuh not to ask about what he did not know [c4]. Nuh asked God to forgive him and to have mercy on him [c5].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that Nuh, when corrected, sought refuge in God and asked for forgiveness [c4][c5].

### What the sources do not establish

- Not established: what the words not of your family mean in detail; readers differ on whether they speak of kinship, of belief or of conduct.
- Not established: whether Nuh was asking for his son's rescue, for forgiveness for him, or for something else; the ayah says only that his son was of his family and that God's promise is true.
- Not established: what the matter was that was decided, or how many were aboard the ship.
- Not established: where the Judi is.
